info.description: Free instant hosting for HTML, Markdown, JSON, key-value stores, files and sites. Omitted ns: private. MCP omission: a generated private namespace. Send ns=public for gallery & search; password, hidden and private publications are excluded. A private link is not a lock: anyone with it can open it; add a password to restrict. Secrets allowed; likely ones are flagged in notices. For a secret: private namespace + password. Retain returned links and owner tokens. manageUrl is private: give it only to the owner, never publish it. How BrewPage compares with GitHub Pages, GitHub Gist, Netlify Drop, Cloudflare Drop, Tiiny Host and Static.app: https://brewpage.app/compare. Agents: remote MCP at https://brewpage.app/mcp (no auth).

post.description: Stores a file via multipart upload and returns a download link. Only safe file types accepted; a missing or wrong extension is corrected from the content and reported in notices. Reuse existing owner token to group entities under one owner. A UTF-8 .html/.htm file sent to namespace 'public' without a password is published as an HTML page (same rules and limits as POST /api/html): link and ownerLink point to the page, notice 'html-file-as-page'. Any other HTML file is stored as a file and shown as source, notice 'html-file-as-source'; to publish such a page use POST /api/html Secrets allowed; likely ones are flagged in notices. For a secret: private namespace + password.

parameters.description: ns=public: the page is listed in the public gallery and the sitemap, so Google, Bing and AI search can find and index it and people can discover it. Use it for anything meant to be found or shared: docs, guides, demos, portfolios, reports, landing pages. Public pages are served right on the brewpage.app domain, which gives them the strongest reach in search; a page whose code needs its own origin (cookies, storage) gets its own subdomain automatically. Anyone can find and read a public page: never put secrets, tokens or personal data there. No ns (default): private. Unlisted and not indexed; anyone who has the link can still open it. Lowercase only.
